item.title: Ep 1 · Ch 1 — From Behavioral Bargain to Attachment Bond
item.description:
Chapter 1: The Field of Couple Therapy and EFT
Traces the paradigm shift that made EFT possible: the relationship is no longer a contract to be renegotiated with communication skills but an emotional bond built on the mammalian need for proximity and safety. The listener learns to abandon the skill-building reflex, read a partner's nagging or withdrawal as an attachment cry, and use Tango Move 1 to reframe the negative cycle as the couple's common enemy.

item.title: Ep 2 · Ch 1 — Separation Distress: When Isolation Registers as Danger
item.description:
Chapter 1: The Field of Couple Therapy and EFT
Unpacks the neurobiology behind EFT's claim that isolation is a biological hazard, from cortisol spikes and amygdala hijack to the tranquilizing effect of a secure bond's nurturant solace. The listener learns to track physiological markers of alarm in session, normalize panic rather than cognitively reframe it, and use RISSSC and Affect Assembly to become a temporary safe haven until the partner can take over that role.

item.title: Ep 3 · Ch 2 — Ten Tenets of Adult Love and Constructive Dependency
item.description:
Chapter 2: An Attachment View of Love: The EFT Approach
Walks through Johnson's ten tenets of adult attachment, showing why secure dependence and autonomy are two sides of one coin rather than opposites. Listeners learn to spot proximity seeking and working models of self and other in session, and to substitute the A.R.E. question (accessible, responsive, engaged) for communication-skills coaching.

item.title: Ep 4 · Ch 2 — Isolation as Trauma: Protest, Despair, and the Freeze Response
item.description:
Chapter 2: An Attachment View of Love: The EFT Approach
Frames attachment theory as a theory of trauma, recasting relationship distress as a wound to the bond rather than a conflict to be mediated. Listeners learn to hear relentless protest as a bid to wake a non-responsive attachment figure, to read shutdown as a freeze response rather than indifference, and to use deepening and enactment to turn a survival move into an attachment signal.

item.title: Ep 5 · Ch 3 — Reprocessing the Felt Sense in the Present Moment
item.description:
Chapter 3: The EFT Theory of Change: Within and Between
Unpacks EFT's humanistic experiential roots — the therapist as process consultant rather than expert analyst, empathy as a "revelation" that orders inner chaos, and secondary emotion as the gateway to primary emotion. Listeners learn the Move 2 affect-deepening pivot and why insight into the past is not the same as emotional change.

item.title: Ep 6 · Ch 3 — Circular Causality and the Cycle as Common Enemy
item.description:
Chapter 3: The EFT Theory of Change: Within and Between
Explores EFT's systemic half — interactional positions, demand-withdraw sequences, and the self-reinforcing feedback loop where each partner's protective move pulls for the other's alarm. Listeners learn how to reframe linear blame into circular awareness and reorganize the system rather than fix a personality flaw.

item.title: Ep 7 · Ch 4 — The Five Moves of the EFT Tango
item.description:
Chapter 4: The Basics of EFT Interventions: Emotions and the Macro-Intervention, the EFT Tango
Walks through the EFT Tango as a macro-intervention: mirroring present process, affect assembly, choreographing an engaged encounter, processing it, then integrating and validating. Listeners learn how to tell when emotion is assembled enough to launch an enactment, and why skipping straight to Move 3 stalls second-order change.

item.title: Ep 8 · Ch 4 — Assembling Emotion: Trigger, Body, Meaning, Action Tendency
item.description:
Chapter 4: The Basics of EFT Interventions: Emotions and the Macro-Intervention, the EFT Tango
Breaks emotion into its five working parts - trigger, initial perception, body response, meaning, and action tendency - and shows how the therapist reassembles them into a coherent attachment signal. Includes the probes that turn a vague reaction into a vivid one, and why trainees most often miss the action tendency.

item.title: Ep 9 · Ch 5 — RISSSC: The Therapist's Voice as Safe Haven
item.description:
Chapter 5: Basic EFT Micro Skills: Experiential and Systemic
Breaks down the six elements of RISSSC (repeat, images, simple, slow, soft, client's words) and how the therapist's voice regulates arousal so clients can approach frightening emotion. Covers the proxy-voice move and the trap of retreating into abstract, professional language.

item.title: Ep 10 · Ch 5 — Enactments as Exposure: Choreographing and Processing Encounters
item.description:
Chapter 5: Basic EFT Micro Skills: Experiential and Systemic
Walks through Tango Moves 3 and 4 — directing a partner to share new vulnerability face-to-face, then processing what it was like to reach and to respond. Includes slicing the risk thinner, enacting the block, and 'catching the bullet' when a partner dismisses the reach.

item.title: Ep 11 · Ch 6 — The Alliance as Secure Base During Assessment
item.description:
Chapter 6: Assessment: Defining the Dance and Listening to the Music
How the first EFT sessions build a therapeutic alliance that both partners experience as safe enough to expose vulnerability, and how the therapist screens for contraindications like ongoing abuse, undisclosed secrets, or incompatible therapy agendas. Listeners learn to read the couple's positioning and automaticity as data, and to validate each partner's moves as legitimate solutions to attachment pain.

item.title: Ep 12 · Ch 6 — Mapping the Dance: Reading the Markers Beneath a Complaint
item.description:
Chapter 6: Assessment: Defining the Dance and Listening to the Music
How to build a topographic map of a couple's negative interaction cycle by tracking intrapsychic markers (unowned affect, rigidly held beliefs) and interpersonal markers (position, distance, exits). Listeners learn to catch the trigger, perception, and action tendency hiding beneath a surface complaint about dishes or in-laws, so the couple stops arguing about content and starts seeing the pattern that runs them both.

item.title: Ep 13 · Ch 7 — Beneath the Blame: Leading a Partner One Step Deeper
item.description:
Chapter 7: Changing the Music: Toward De-Escalation/Stabilization
How to run Tango Move 2 (affect assembly and deepening) by tracking trigger, perception, body response, meaning, and action tendency, then using RISSSC and empathic conjecture to lead a partner one step deeper rather than ten. Listeners learn why reframing hostility as an "urgent search" for connection works where ventilating raw emotion does not.

item.title: Ep 14 · Ch 7 — Step 4 De-escalation: The Couple Takes the Meta-View
item.description:
Chapter 7: Changing the Music: Toward De-Escalation/Stabilization
What Step 4 de-escalation actually looks like in the room: the couple rises above the fight, names the pattern together, and stops holding each other responsible for it. Covers Tango Move 5 (summarizing and consolidating), validating the withdrawer's paralysis, and "catching the bullet" of a listening partner's skepticism to protect a vulnerable disclosure.

item.title: Ep 15 · Ch 8 — Protection Becomes a Prison: The Withdrawer Re-engages
item.description:
Chapter 8: Deepening Engagement: The Beginning of Stage 2
How Step 5 works for the withdrawer: helping him own the strategy behind the numbness ("I hide so I don't hear that I failed") and turn that disowned attachment fear into an assertive, engaged disclosure. Covers Tango Moves 2 and 3, slicing risk thinner, and why the withdrawer is engaged before the pursuer softens.

item.title: Ep 16 · Ch 8 — Catching the Bullet When the Listener Won't Believe
item.description:
Chapter 8: Deepening Engagement: The Beginning of Stage 2
Step 6 from the observing partner's seat: why a heartfelt disclosure often meets skepticism, testing, or contempt, and how the therapist validates that disbelief without abandoning the partner who just risked. Includes catching the bullet, normalizing mistrust as a survival strategy, and processing the encounter so working models can actually shift.

item.title: Ep 17 · Ch 9 — The Withdrawer's Assertive Reach: Stepping Out of Hiding
item.description:
Chapter 9: Reaching for Secure Connection
How Step 7 turns a placating, silent partner into someone who states terms and needs from an empowered position, and why trainees mistake that new firmness for hostility. Covers choreographing the engaged encounter, heightening the reach, and the markers that re-engagement is complete.

item.title: Ep 18 · Ch 9 — Pursuer Softening: Putting Down the Shield of Anger
item.description:
Chapter 9: Reaching for Secure Connection
Walks through EFT's signature change event, where the blaming partner faces the 'dragon' of self-criticism and asks for comfort from vulnerability instead of protesting. Explains RISSSC, seeding attachment, and why softening the pursuer before the withdrawer has re-engaged compounds the injury.

item.title: Ep 19 · Ch 10 — Old Problems Dissolve When Attachment Fear Leaves the Room
item.description:
Chapter 10: The Consolidation of a Secure Base: Stage 3
Step 8 shows why couples suddenly solve pragmatic issues like money or work hours once those issues stop symbolizing rejection, and why EFT deliberately teaches no problem-solving skills. Listeners learn to spot consolidation markers, use Tango Move 5 to integrate and validate the couple's own solutions, and help them build a coherent narrative of how they changed.

item.title: Ep 20 · Ch 10 — Scaffolding a Life on the Bond: Ending Therapy
item.description:
Chapter 10: The Consolidation of a Secure Base: Stage 3
Step 9 and termination: how to recognize when a couple is ready to fly on their own, work with their healthy trepidation, and refuse credit for their success. Listeners learn to build rituals of greeting and leaving, audit schedules so the relationship stays figural rather than background, and plan for the old cycle's return.

item.title: Ep 21 · Ch 11 — Alliance, Not Distress, Predicts Who Succeeds
item.description:
Chapter 11: Key Clinical Issues and Solutions: Becoming an EFT Therapist
Why the therapeutic bond and the perceived relevance of tasks forecast EFT outcomes far better than a couple's initial level of distress, and why inexpressive partners often thrive when the therapist works as a surrogate processor. Also covers the prognostic markers worth tracking, the EFT stance on diversity, and why emotional disengagement is the most dangerous sign of all.

item.title: Ep 22 · Ch 11 — Lost in Content: Returning to the Emotional Thread
item.description:
Chapter 11: Key Clinical Issues and Solutions: Becoming an EFT Therapist
How trainees slip from process consultant into referee, and the move back: returning to the last poignant emotional moment, using RISSSC, and shifting from intrapsychic exploration to interpersonal enactment. Includes handling the reluctance to enact and spotting when a client's story sparks the therapist's own attachment wounds.

item.title: Ep 23 · Ch 12 — Reading the Symptom as an Attachment Protest
item.description:
Chapter 12: EFFT: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
How EFFT reframes an adolescent's bulimia or depression as a protest against a parent's inaccessibility rather than an individual disorder, and how the EFT Tango is used to shift the child-parent cycle of aggressive criticism and withdrawn distance. Listeners learn why the secure base is the parent's job to build, and why children must connect before they can leave.

item.title: Ep 24 · Ch 12 — Working Through Parental Shame to Reach the Child
item.description:
Chapter 12: EFFT: Emotionally Focused Family Therapy
Why a parent's cool distance or agitation is usually a shield forged from shame and fear of having failed, and how the therapist gives the parent a safe haven first so they can tolerate their child's anger. Listeners learn the parent-side withdrawer re-engagement, catching the bullet, and the bonding enactment that invites a child from attack to soft reach.

item.title: Ep 25 · Ch 13 — The Never Again Wound: Attachment Injuries as Trauma
item.description:
Chapter 13: Relationship Traumas: Addressing Attachment Injuries
How a betrayal at a moment of acute need becomes a relationship trauma that blocks de-escalation, showing up in-session as hypervigilance, secondary anger, and refusal to risk. Listeners learn to name the injury, assemble its raw affect, and recognize why logic ("that was ten years ago") never dissolves it.

item.title: Ep 26 · Ch 13 — The Vulnerable Apology That Reorganizes the Bond
item.description:
Chapter 13: Relationship Traumas: Addressing Attachment Injuries
Forgiveness in EFT is an emotional reorganization, not a cognitive letting-go: the injuring partner must stay present with the pain and offer remorse without defense or "buts." Listeners learn to choreograph that enactment, process the injured partner's response, and avoid pushing for forgiveness before the hurt has been fully spoken.

item.title: Ep 27 · Ch 14 — Stopping the Content Trap and Naming the Cycle
item.description:
Chapter 14: Live at an EFT Externship: A Stage 1 EFT Session
Walks through Stage 1 de-escalation as it plays out in a live session: how the therapist refuses to referee the content and keeps pivoting to process, mirroring the pursue-withdraw dance in real time. Listeners learn the Move 1 interventions — the process stop, naming the dance as the enemy, and validating each partner's position — and the marker that tells you de-escalation has landed.

item.title: Ep 28 · Ch 14 — Slicing Emotion Thinner With RISSSC and the Echo
item.description:
Chapter 14: Live at an EFT Externship: A Stage 1 EFT Session
Covers affect assembly and deepening: catching the sub-second shifts — a quivering lip, a single loaded word like "invisible" — and using RISSSC to slow the session's tempo and unfold the emotion. Listeners learn to echo the client's words, slice for the split-second feeling that preceded the anger, and build clinical images that make emotion tangible, while avoiding the trainee trap of fixing a feeling before it's felt.

item.title: Ep 29 · Ch 15 — The Softening in Real Time: From Protest to Need
item.description:
Chapter 15: A Stage 2 EFT Session
Walks through the live moment a blaming partner drops the protest and voices vulnerable need directly to their spouse, and why it only lands once the withdrawer is already re-engaged and accessible. Covers the therapist's choreographing of the enactment, catching the client's bolt back into blame, and refusing to settle for a half-reach spoken to the therapist instead of the partner.

item.description:
Chapter 15: A Stage 2 EFT Session
Shows what a restructured bond looks like in session: reciprocal attunement, conflict without escalation, and internal working models shifting from "I am alone" to "we are a team." Covers Move 5 integration, helping the couple narrate their own victory, and knowing when to stop treating and get out of the way.
